presentingComplaint: Day-6 inpatient with new fever, worsening breathlessness and increasing oxygen requirement, on a background of decompensated heart failure.
history: Admitted 6 days ago through the emergency department with acute decompensated heart failure (ischaemic cardiomyopathy, LVEF 30%) precipitated by rapid atrial fibrillation. He was diuresed with IV furosemide with good early response - weight fell 3.2 kg, orthopnoea and leg oedema improved, and oxygen was weaned from 6 L to 2 L by day 3. From the morning of day 5 he became newly febrile, more breathless despite ongoing net-negative fluid balance, and began producing yellow-green sputum, which is a change from his baseline. Nursing staff note thicker, purulent secretions and he needed oxygen escalated back up to 4 L then 6 L. He has type 2 diabetes, CKD stage 3, and had a 5-day course of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection 7 weeks ago. No recent travel. The confounding question on the ward round was whether this simply represents heart-failure decompensation / flash pulmonary oedema rather than a new infection.
examination: Elderly man, mildly confused from baseline, using accessory muscles. Bilateral basal crepitations (long-standing with his heart failure) but NEW coarse bronchial crepitations and increased vocal resonance at the right base. JVP raised at 4 cm (down from admission), trace bilateral ankle oedema, no new gallop. Chest otherwise as before. No calf swelling.

labs.abg: pH 7.42, PaO2 8.1 kPa on 6L, PaCO2 4.6 kPa

imaging: Portable CXR: new dense right lower/mid-zone consolidation with air bronchograms, distinct from the pre-existing upper-zone vascular redistribution and small pleural effusions seen on admission; cardiomegaly stable, no new interstitial oedema pattern to explain the focal opacity. Lung ultrasound: focal subpleural consolidation with dynamic air bronchograms at right base (not a bilateral B-line oedema pattern).
microbiology: Blood cultures x2 sent. Sputum Gram stain: numerous polymorphs with Gram-negative bacilli; culture pending. Nasopharyngeal respiratory viral PCR negative. Legionella and pneumococcal urinary antigens sent.
differentialDiagnoses: Decompensated heart failure / flash pulmonary oedema
finalDiagnosis: Hospital-acquired pneumonia (non-ventilator) developing on day 6 of admission, superimposed on treated decompensated heart failure
citations: IDSA/ATS - Management of Hospital-Acquired and Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia - 2016
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Pneumonia
stewardship: Empiric broad-spectrum therapy for non-ventilator HAP with a single anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam (piperacillin-tazobactam), covering P. aeruginosa and Gram-negative bacilli given onset >48h, recent antibiotic exposure and diabetes/CKD; add MRSA cover only if local MRSA prevalence >20% or prior MRSA. De-escalate on culture and clinical response; reassess at 48-72h and treat for 7 days if responding.
contraindications: Avoid nephrotoxic combinations where possible given CKD stage 3 and rising creatinine - dose-adjust piperacillin-tazobactam and monitor renal function
Avoid empiric fluid boluses / over-hydration given underlying heart failure
Caution with aminoglycosides given renal impairment
edgeCases: Falsely attributing the new focal consolidation to heart-failure decompensation and withholding antibiotics
Bilateral basal crackles from chronic heart failure masking the new focal HAP
Elevated NT-proBNP being over-interpreted as pure cardiac decompensation despite it falling from admission
Distinguishing HAP from early aspiration given confusion and reduced mobility
expectedMaiK: Recognise that a new focal consolidation, purulent secretions, fever, leukocytosis and raised procalcitonin arising >48h after admission indicate hospital-acquired pneumonia rather than heart-failure decompensation alone, and start empiric anti-pseudomonal cover.
expectedNextQuestions: Exact day of admission and timing of symptom onset relative to it (>48h)?
Change in sputum character/volume from baseline?
Prior antibiotic exposure and any prior resistant organisms (MDR risk)?
Local unit antibiogram / MRSA and Pseudomonas prevalence?
Aspiration risk - dysphagia, reduced consciousness, witnessed aspiration?
expectedInvestigations: Lower respiratory tract sample for Gram stain and culture (sputum/tracheal aspirate)
Full blood count, CRP/procalcitonin, renal function and electrolytes
Legionella and pneumococcal urinary antigens; respiratory viral PCR
regressionAssertions: consolidation == true differentiates HAP from pure heart-failure decompensation
heart_failure appears as a differential but is not the final diagnosis
